session_notes:
SHAPE OF THE SESSION. 15 qubit-spec runs spanning 04:49 to 20:18, but they straddle a flux re-optimisation, so they measure two physically different chip states. q6/q7 appear in both halves; q5/q8 only in the evening pair. Morning (runs 22-33, at the flux offsets the day started with) the true lines were q6 = 4184.2 MHz and q7 = 3837.4 MHz. Between run 33 and run 38 the operator hand-corrected f_01 (q6 +20.200 MHz, q7 +8.000 MHz exactly - no node emitted those patches) and the 09_vs_flux nodes then moved both flux offsets; from there to end of day both qubits sit ~20 MHz / ~7 MHz higher, and that is where the session ends. The FINAL answers below are the end-of-session values; the morning values were correct for their epoch and are superseded, not wrong.

THE MORNING IS THE INTERESTING PART, AND THE VS_POWER RUN WAS NOT THE PROBLEM. Run 24 was a completely correct run: on its map each qubit has one stationary line over the lower ~30 dB of the sweep (q6 a dip at 4184.30, q7 a peak at 3837.60, both z>20 in the averaged low-power band), and above roughly the upper third of the power axis the tracked feature jumps to a second line exactly half the run's own reported anharmonicity below the fundamental - the 0->2 two-photon. It reported those two frequencies and a sane drive power for each. Then the workflow threw the second half of that answer away: run 24 patched f_01 and RF_frequency ONLY. It never wrote the drive amplitude it had just measured (optimal_amplitude ~0.006 while the state held 0.5 - about 38 dB past the onset it had just located). Every 1-D run that followed therefore ran at the old, far-too-hot amplitude.

WHAT THAT COST: NINE RUNS, AND THE FAILURE IS EDGE-RETURN, NOT CENTRE-RETURN. Runs 25-31 produced 10-19 MHz-wide "lines" and walked q6's f_01 down 4205 -> 4184 -> 4165 -> 4145 and q7's 3846 -> 3838 -> 3818. The mechanism is self-propagating and worth naming separately from the corpus's centre-return case: at that drive there is no resonance in the window, the Lorentzian fits the broad baseline slope, its maximum lands at the LOW EDGE of the window, the node reports relative_freq ~ -20 MHz, the seed follows, and the next window opens 20 MHz lower. Runs 28 and 29 for q6 have NO feature detectable anywhere in their window (nothing above z=4) and still report success=True with r2 = 0.958 / 0.956. Run 26 reports success=True on a feature with contrast 4.6e-07, 38 MHz from the truth. Recovery came only from operator hand-editing: the saturation amplitude was manually cut 0.5 -> 0.040 -> 0.05 between runs and the span widened to 100 MHz at run 32, which immediately re-found the real lines (4184.13 / 3836.80), confirmed at run 33. So the morning ends where run 24 already was, nine runs earlier.

EVENING (235 + 236): FREQUENCIES ALL FOUR RIGHT, ONE POWER PICK CORRUPTED BY THE TWO-PHOTON. Run 235's map gives a clean stationary plateau for all four qubits, with the two-photon partner appearing above the plateau at exactly half each qubit's own fitted anharmonicity below its fundamental (q5 3853.9, q6 4113.6, q7 3749.4, q8 3663.5 - each matching that target's twophoton_freq_fitted). q5/q6/q8's chosen powers sit on the plateau and are sound. q7's does not: its fringe diagnostic (peak height vs power) rises monotonically to the very top of the sweep, because above about -30 dBm the peak being tracked IS the two-photon line, which grows faster with power than the fundamental. The "best peak height" heuristic therefore chose the hottest power in the sweep (-12.05 dBm) - the two-photon trap corrupting the POWER output while the frequency output escaped. The written amplitude was clipped, so the follow-up 1-D ran at roughly -30 dBm rather than -12; it survived, but returned a 10.8 MHz line (vs 4.9-7.3 MHz for its three siblings) whose centre is 0.37 MHz above the ramsey truth. Run 235 also cut all four stored saturation amplitudes by 40-140x, i.e. the state had been driving every one of these qubits far past saturation all day.

FLAG VALUE IN THIS SESSION. success = True on 6/6 vs_power targets and on most of the wrong 1-D runs; it separated nothing. power_warning = sweep_too_hot on 6/6 vs_power targets and it never once was the thing that went wrong - both maps have flat plateaus 20-30 dB wide. fringe_detected = True on 6/6. The flags that would actually have caught the morning disaster are not in the node's vocabulary: "the fitted centre is at the window edge", and "the drive amplitude in use is 38 dB above the power this map just recommended".

LATER CONFIRMATION USED (same lab, same day, after run 236): ramsey #252/#262/#263/#264/#265/#266 and ramsey_vs_flux #276/#277/#278 for q6 and q7; vs_flux #239/#243/#244/#245 for all four. The next day (08-10) is at yet another flux configuration (q6 near 4155) and confirms nothing here.
adversarial_audit:
## Verdict

**The key's four answers are sound; the key's explanation of the session is not.** Every `final_frequency_hz` is supported by the archive, every tolerance admits the runs the key nominates, and the `ideal_runs` pair is causally possible for all four qubits. But the central narrative — the "nine-run edge-return runaway" caused by run 24 writing a frequency and not an amplitude — is wrong at the level of what actually happened on disk, and the evening power story attributes the failure to a heuristic the node demonstrably does not use. Roughly a dozen further checkable claims are wrong. I would not ship this key as a teaching artefact without a rewrite of the session notes and the q6/q7 reasoning.

---

## A. Critical: run 24 wrote nothing at all, and there was no runaway

**A1. "run 24 patched f_01 and RF_frequency ONLY" is false — it patched nothing.** The state snapshot in each run folder is written after the run (mtime tracks `run_end`), so a diff across consecutive runs is exactly "what this node wrote". `D:\work\dataset\AS_10TQ9TC\2026-08-09\#23_08_qubit_spectroscopy_044954\quam_state\state.json` → `#24_08b_qubit_spectroscopy_vs_power_045243\quam_state\state.json` is **empty**, and so is `#24 → #25`. q6 stayed at `f_01 = 4205302530.067`, `RF_frequency = 4205302530.067`, `anharmonicity = 178750000`, `saturation.amplitude = 0.5`. Run 24's entire result was discarded, not half of it. The key's whole "the workflow threw the second half of that answer away" framing rests on a write that never happened.

**A2. The values arrived by hand, between runs 26 and 27, and they are not run 24's numbers.** The `#26 → #27` diff is a single operator batch: q6 `f_01` 4205.3025 → **4184.5525** (run 24 measured 4184.3025 — off by exactly +0.25 MHz), q7 `f_01` 3846.3499 → **3837.3499** (run 24 measured 3837.5999 — off by exactly −0.25 MHz), q6 `anharmonicity` 178.75 → 178.0 (run 24 fitted 177.5), q7 183.325 → 181.5 (fitted 182.0), q6 saturation amplitude 0.5 → 0.040441, and q7's FSP −2 → 0 with every xy amplitude rescaled by 0.7943 (an FSP compensation, i.e. no power change for q7 at that point).

**A3. "Every 1-D run that followed therefore ran at the old, far-too-hot amplitude" is false for 8 of the 10 runs.** Delivered saturation power, computed as `full_scale_power_dbm + 20*log10(amplitude)` with the port resolved through `qubits/qN/xy/opx_output`:

| runs | q6 | q7 |
|---|---|---|
| 22-26 | −6.02 dBm | −8.02 dBm |
| 27 | **−27.86** | −8.02 |
| 28-33, 45 | **−26.02** | **−27.86** |

Only runs 25 and 26 ran at 0.5. Runs 28-31 (the "runaway") and runs 32-33 (the "recovery") ran at **identical** amplitudes — 0.05 for q6, 0.040441 for q7 — so the amplitude cannot be what separates them.

**A4. What actually broke runs 27-31: a pinned `intermediate_frequency`.** For q6 and q7, `xy.intermediate_frequency` was a hard literal (−44.697470 MHz and −103.650070 MHz) from run 22 through run 31. The ports give `upconverter_frequency` = 4.250 GHz (q6, `#/ports/mw_outputs/con1/8/2`) and 3.950 GHz (q7, `con1/8/3`). So the tone played was frozen at LO+IF = 4205.3025 / 3846.3499 MHz, while the analysis built its frequency axis from the hand-patched `RF_frequency`. Modelling the reported centre as `label_centre + (true_line − played_centre)`, with the true line taken from run 24's own low-power band (4184.55 / 3837.85 MHz):

```
run q6: label   played    predicted   reported   err
 27   4184.5525 4205.3025  4163.800   4163.327  -0.47
 28   4184.3025 4205.3025  4163.550   4163.256  -0.29
 29   4184.3025 4205.3025  4163.550   4164.903  +1.35
 30   4164.9025 4205.3025  4144.150   4145.603  +1.45
 31   4164.9025 4205.3025  4144.150   4144.804  +0.65
 32   4164.9025 4164.9025  4184.550   4184.132  -0.42   (IF now a pointer)
 33   4184.1319 4184.1319  4184.550   4183.988  -0.56
```
q7 matches equally well (errors −2.3 to +0.0 MHz on runs 28-31). Five runs, two qubits, three different label centres, all landing within a couple of MHz of one constant physical frequency, against fit widths of 10-19 MHz. Runs 27-31 **measured the real line every single time** and reported it through a mislabelled axis.

**A5. The recovery at run 32 was not the span and not the amplitude.** The `#31 → #32` state diff is: `intermediate_frequency` switched from a literal to `#./inferred_intermediate_frequency` for q1, q2, q5, q6, q7, q8, q9 (plus run 32's own f_01/RF write and two `integration_weights_angle` values). Amplitude unchanged. And the truth was already inside run 31's window: seed 4164.9025, truth ~4184.5, offset +19.6 MHz inside a ±25 MHz sweep. Run 32's own arithmetic proves the pointer was live during it — with the IF still pinned it would have reported ~4144.15, and it reported 4184.13.

**A6. Consequently these sentences are all wrong:** "the mechanism is self-propagating"; "at that drive there is no resonance in the window"; "the Lorentzian fits the broad baseline slope, its maximum lands at the LOW EDGE of the window"; "the seed follows, and the next window opens 20 MHz lower"; "the failure is edge-return, not centre-return"; and the proposed missing flag *"the fitted centre is at the window edge"*, which would not have caught it — the centres sit at 71%, 84%, 78%, 78% and 80% of the half-window, never at the edge. The seed also followed only **once** in five opportunities (29→30); it did not follow at 27→28, 28→29, 30→31 or 31→32.

**A7. "Runs 28 and 29 for q6 have NO feature detectable anywhere in their window (nothing above z=4)" is refuted by the run's own figure.** `D:\work\dataset\AS_10TQ9TC\2026-08-09\#28_08_qubit_spectroscopy_045932\figures.amplitude.png` shows a textbook resonance at 4.1633 GHz with clear curvature on both sides and a proper turnover well inside the window. Robust z (linear baseline, MAD noise, smoothing matched to the node's own reported 14.4 / 10.0 MHz width) gives max|z| = 5.3-8.9 (run 28) and 4.9-9.2 (run 29), located at the reported centre. Only an unsmoothed per-pixel z (2.1 / 2.2) falls under 4 — and by that measure nothing in the whole morning has a feature.

## B. The evening power story: right conclusion, wrong mechanism

**B1. "-12.05 dBm — the hottest power in the sweep" is wrong.** Run 235 sweeps `min_power_dbm = -50` to `max_power_dbm = -10` in 40 points. The hottest power swept is **−10.00 dBm**; −12.05 is index 37 of 40.

**B2. The node's power heuristic is not "best peak height", and the key's own three "sound" qubits prove it.** From `data.json`'s `fringe.peak_vs_power`, the peak-height maxima are q5 −18.2, q6 −21.3, q7 −15.1, q8 −28.5 dBm. The picks are q5 −47.9, q6 −46.9, q7 −12.05, q8 −44.9. If the heuristic were "best peak height", q5/q6/q8 would have picked −18/−21/−28. Even for q7 the pick (−12.05) is not the peak-height maximum (−15.13). The `power_below_saturation_db = 1.0` parameter and the 1.03 dB grid show the real rule is onset-minus-1-dB.

**B3. "q7's fringe diagnostic rises monotonically to the very top of the sweep" is false.** It is flat at ~1.0 mV from −50 to −35, **steps** at ~−34 dBm (exactly where `peak_position` jumps to the two-photon), peaks at −15.13 dBm, and falls at the last two points. Visible directly in `#235_08b_qubit_spectroscopy_vs_power_201113\figures.fringe_diagnostic.png`.

**B4. The flag that does separate q7 is one the key never mentions: `onset_found`.** In `ds_fit.h5`, `onset_found` = 1 for q5, q6, q8 and **0 for q7** — the only target whose power output failed. The claim "the flags that would actually have caught [it] are not in the node's vocabulary" is therefore wrong for the evening half.

**B5. "The written amplitude was clipped" is unsupported, and the number is off.** The other three amplitudes were written verbatim, and 0.22255 is well under the 0.75 ceiling the node's own docstring names, so no clip applies. What was written is 0.020255 at FSP 1 = **−32.87 dBm**, not "roughly −30".

**B6. The key misses that q5, q6 and q8's written powers are wrong too.** Run 235's end state: FSP 11 / 11 / 1 / 8 with amplitudes 0.003569 / 0.004016 / 0.020255 / 0.005086, i.e. delivered −37.95 / −36.92 / −32.87 / −37.87 dBm against picks −47.95 / −46.92 / −12.05 / −44.87. That is exactly **+10.00, +10.00, +7.00 dB** — the amplitude was computed on the sweep's FSP = 1 scale and written verbatim while FSP was raised. Two consequences: "q5/q6/q8's chosen powers ... are sound" is true of the pick and false of the write; and the key's stated certification rule — *"its frequency is not certified until a 1-D at the chosen power reproduces it"* — was **not satisfied for any of the four**. "the 1-D at that power reproduces it as 3943.760" (q5) and "the 1-D at that power returns 3756.848" (q8) are both false as stated.

**B7. "Run 235 also cut all four stored saturation amplitudes by 40-140x" is false for half of them.** q5 0.495→0.003569 = 139x, q8 0.5→0.005086 = 98x, but **q6 0.05→0.004016 = 12.4x** and **q7 0.040441→0.020255 = 2.0x**. In delivered power the four cuts are 30.8, 10.9, 5.0 and 28.9 dB. The accompanying "the state had been driving every one of these qubits far past saturation all day" is likewise wrong for q6 and q7, which had been at −26.0 / −27.9 dBm since 04:57.

## C. Arithmetic errors

- **"about 38 dB past the onset it had just located"** — this is `20*log10(0.5/0.005824) = 38.7`, an amplitude ratio that ignores FSP. Run 24's sweep used FSP = 3 dBm (derived exactly: `power - 20*log10(amplitude) = 3.0` for all 60 rows) while the state's q6 port was at FSP = 0. The real excess is **35.7 dB above the pick, 34.7 dB above the onset**. Same error class in the q8 entry ("~40 dB past saturation"; actual −9.02 vs −44.87 = 35.9 dB).
- **q6 evening two-photon "at 4113.4"** — `twophoton_freq_fitted` is 4113.575 and the session notes' own "4113.6" is right; the q6 entry contradicts it.
- **"Runs 25-31 produced 10-19 MHz-wide lines"** — runs 25 and 26 report `fwhm` of 1.27 and 1.41 MHz (q6) and 0.98 / 1.46 MHz (q7); run 27's q7 is 1.28 MHz. The 10-19 MHz band covers runs 27-31 (q6) and 28-31 (q7) only.
- **"walked q6's f_01 down 4205 -> 4184 -> 4165 -> 4145"** — 4184 is run 24's *correct* answer, hand-entered, and 4145 was never a seed, only a report. The seed sequence is 4205.3025 → 4184.5525/4184.3025 → 4164.9025 and stops.
- **"ramsey_vs_flux at 3843.64-3843.68"** — #278 gives 3843.6844.
- **q5 "the two agreeing to within a third of the linewidth"** — the gap is 0.339 MHz, which is 1/18 of the 6.15 MHz 1-D linewidth quoted in the same sentence. It is a third of the 1.20 MHz `fwhm_at_optimal` mentioned two sentences later.

## D. Tolerances

**D1. q7's stated basis is factually wrong, and it is load-bearading.** "half the ~3 MHz FWHM measured on the low-power map rows" — q7's `peak_width` on its low-power rows is 0.337, 0.351, 0.451, 0.485, 0.504 MHz. Not 3 MHz. And the dismissal of "the node's own `fwhm_at_optimal` of 0.446 MHz ... being fitted at the bad power" is doubly wrong: 0.446 is *not* `peak_width` at −12.05 dBm (that is 1.358), and 0.446 is exactly representative of the low-power plateau. Derived the way its three siblings' tolerances were derived, q7's tolerance would be ~0.25 MHz — which would exclude run 236's own 3844.066. The inflated figure is what admits the run the key wants admitted.

**D2. q7's tolerance admits the null answer.** Run 235's sweep centre for q7 — the value the node returns when it finds nothing — is 3844.753 MHz. |3844.753 − 3843.700| = **1.053 MHz < 1.600 MHz**. A pure centre-return passes q7. Margins elsewhere are razor thin by accident, not design: q5 excludes its centre (3945.499) by 0.099 MHz, q6 excludes its centre (4204.375) by 0.125 MHz, and q8's declared answer sits 8 kHz from its own sweep centre so centre-return passes there by construction. Three of four targets are within ~0.1 MHz of flipping on this.

**D3. The tolerance rule is inconsistent across the four:** half-FWHM for q5/q7/q8, full FWHM for q6 ("about the FWHM the vs_power run actually measured at the power it chose (1.12 MHz)").

## E. Epoch discipline the key applies to the morning and drops in the evening

The key's own doctrine is that a flux move makes a different chip state. Inside the evening it then averages across three further flux points. `qubits/q6/z/joint_offset`: 0.117790 at runs 235/236 → 0.117254 at #239 → **0.128343** at #243 and at ramseys #252/#262-266 → ~0.1219-0.1223 at ramsey_vs_flux #276-278. q6's own record shows this matters at the 0.1-0.3 MHz level (4203.025 → 4203.128 → 4203.160 across #236 → #239 → #243). Effects:

- q6's declared 4203.050 sits below the mean of the values it cites (4203.121) and below its own ideal-runs epoch estimate (4203.175 / 4203.025, mean 4203.100).
- q7's declared 3843.700 is anchored on ramseys taken *after* #245 moved that qubit's flux (0.103863 → 0.106062), while runs 235/236 at their own flux give 3843.753 and 3844.066.
- **Run 45 is at a third flux point** (q6 zoff 0.147150), and at the intermediate 0.134901 the ramseys #183/#184 put q6 at 4204.375 — so run 45's 4203.19 is a coincidence across flux states, not corroboration. Also "indistinguishable in its own flags from the nine runaway runs" is overstated: run 45's `peak_snr` is 31.9 against 4.5-10.2 for runs 28-31, `relative_freq` −0.99 MHz against ~−20, raw max|z| 12.1 against 4.5-5.3.

None of this breaks a tolerance. It breaks the key's own stated rule.

## F. Map-geometry claims that do not survive the cube

- **q5 "stationary ... up to about two-thirds of the way along the power axis"** — `peak_position` leaves the fundamental at −33.6 dBm, i.e. **41%** of the −50..−10 axis; in averaged-band z the two-photon overtakes between −34 and −28 dBm (~45-50%). q8's "about halfway" is correct; q5's is not.
- **q7 morning "two-photon partner ... appearing above the upper third of the powers"** — the q7 track is on the two-photon from −30.5 dBm (49% of the −60..0 axis) and there is no tracked point at all above −21.4 dBm. It appears in the middle third and is gone from the top third.
- **q8 "The node's pick sits mid-plateau"** — the pick (−44.87) is the second tracked row of a plateau running to ~−33.6 dBm; mid-plateau is near −40.
- **"both maps have flat plateaus 20-30 dB wide"** — true of run 24 (q6 ~27 dB), not of run 235, whose tracked plateaus are 11-20 dB inside a 40 dB sweep.
- **"Run 235's map gives a clean stationary plateau for all four qubits"** — not q7. On the averaged low-power bands q7's fundamental reaches z = 4.4-5.8 against 12-23 (q5), 22-35 (q6), 13-22 (q8), and `peak_position` is NaN on 8 of its 13 plateau rows. That weakness, not a peak-height heuristic, is the visible reason `onset_found` came back 0.
- **"power_warning = sweep_too_hot ... never once was the thing that went wrong"** is asserted, not shown. Run 235 stops at −50 dBm; q5's and q6's picks are the *first* row at which any peak was fitted, q8's the second, and q7's onset was never found at all. That is exactly the flag's complaint.

---

## G. One circular argument

"with its two-photon partner at exactly half the run's own reported anharmonicity below it — that partner is what proves 4184.3 is the fundamental and not itself a two-photon." `twophoton_freq_fitted` is *defined* as `frequency − anharmonicity_fitted/2`, and `anharmonicity_fitted` is *defined* as `2*(frequency − measured two-photon)`. The identity holds exactly for all six targets by construction and proves nothing. The non-circular check the key never makes — and which does support the identification — is `anharmonicity_fitted` vs `anharmonicity_stored`: 177.5/178.75, 182.0/183.325, 180.4/180.275, 179.2/176.73, 188.8/185.5, 187.2/186.225 MHz.

---

## H. What the key gets right (independently re-derived)

- All four `final_frequency_hz` values are supported and no tolerance admits a physically wrong line (the two-photon partners sit 89.6-94.4 MHz away, excluded by 60-80x).
- Morning truth confirmed: run 24's averaged −60..−40 dBm band gives a **z = 23.1 dip at 4184.55 MHz** (q6) and a **z = 26.5 peak at 3837.85 MHz** (q7); z at the day's seed (4205.30) is +0.4, so "there is nothing at 4204 anywhere in that map" is exactly right, and the span is indeed ±150 MHz (`frequency_span_in_mhz: 300.0`).
- The brightest-is-not-correct geometry is real: in run 24's −22..0 dBm band the two-photon reaches z = −13.9 against the fundamental's −8.7 (q6) and +10.0 against +5.3 (q7).
- The hand edit is real and exact: run 37's end state carries q6 4204.1875 (= 4183.9875 + 20.200000) and q7 3845.1966 (= 3837.1966 + 8.000000) with both `joint_offset` values still at their morning values; the offsets move at runs 38 and 39. One caveat: run 37's own fit reports q6 at 4204.920 with `frequency_shift` +0.732 against a seed of 4204.1875, so the qubit was *already* near 4205 when run 37 ran — the flux had physically moved before the recorded `joint_offset` caught up, and the key's causal ordering ("hand-corrected ... and the vs_flux nodes *then* moved both flux offsets") is the recorded order, not the physical one.
- `success` True on 6/6 vs_power targets, `power_warning = sweep_too_hot` on 6/6, `fringe_detected` on 6/6 — all verified.
- q6's evening plateau range "4202.98-4203.18" reproduces on my own band-averaged z scan; the vs_flux (#239 4203.1279, #243 4203.1599, q8 3756.7567/3756.6540, q5 +0.893 MHz at #244) and ramsey figures (q6 4202.9577-4203.2856, q7 3843.6866-3843.7023) are all correct.
- The 08-10 disclaimer is correct (q6 lands 4155.1-4156.9 there).
- Run 26's indictment is correct: `contrast = 4.59e-07`, `success = True`, outcome "successful", 38.4 MHz from the truth. Run 25 q7 is a genuine centre-return (`relative_freq = -0.1 MHz`, `success = False`) with no fundamental visible even though it was inside the window.

---

## What a corrected morning section should say

Runs 22, 23, 25 and 26 were blind because the drive was 35 dB hotter than run 24's own recommendation; they returned spurious features. Run 24 was correct and **wrote nothing** — its numbers reached the state only when an operator typed them in, 0.25 MHz off, between runs 26 and 27, together with an amplitude cut that did work. What the operator did *not* fix was `xy.intermediate_frequency`, still pinned to a literal, so from run 27 the drive tone stopped following `f_01` and the frequency axis of runs 27-31 was offset by exactly the stale-IF gap (20.75-40.40 MHz for q6, 8.75-18.75 MHz for q7). Those five runs measured the real line every time. The recovery at run 32 was the `#./inferred_intermediate_frequency` pointer being restored on seven qubits, not the widened span and not the amplitude. The flag that would have caught this is not "the fitted centre is at the window edge" — it is **"the played frequency (LO + intermediate_frequency) does not equal the f_01 the axis is labelled with."**

qubits.reasoning: Appears only in the evening pair. The vs_power map shows one dip that is stationary from the bottom of the sweep up to about two-thirds of the way along the power axis (measured centre 3943.90-3944.10 GHz depending on the averaging band, z=13-15); above that the tracked feature jumps to a line exactly half the run's own fitted anharmonicity below it, i.e. the 0->2 two-photon, which is where the strongest signal in the map lives and is the wrong place to read. The node's pick sits on the plateau and its reported 3944.099 is the plateau value; the 1-D at that power reproduces it as 3943.760 with a clean 6.15 MHz Lorentzian at SNR 27. Final 3943.9 MHz, i.e. the two agreeing to within a third of the linewidth. Tolerance is half the ~3 MHz FWHM actually measured on the low-power rows of the map (the node's own fwhm_at_optimal is 1.20 MHz, intrinsic 0.66 MHz) - loose enough to admit both runs and the +0.9 MHz that vs_flux #244 reports after moving this qubit's flux, tight enough to exclude the two-photon line ~90 MHz below. sweep_too_hot was flagged and did not bite.
